questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A critique of Bhutan's monarchy and its handling of tourism during Covid
A guide to the top hotels and restaurants for first-time visitors to Bhutan
A detailed history of how Bhutan resisted annexation by China and India
The author's impressions of Bhutan, a long-wished-for destination with unusual customs
questions.explain: The author describes visiting Bhutan, a country at the top of his list, and what makes it special.

questions.q: How did the author and his wife plan to travel before Covid and the babies?
options: Visit one new continent each year
Visit two new countries every year
Take one long trip every other year
Visit a country from The List each month
questions.explain: Early on they pledged to visit two new countries every year.

questions.q: Which environmental fact does the passage state about Bhutan?
options: It is carbon-negative because its forests absorb more CO2 than its people emit
It bans TV and internet to preserve tradition and reduce modern impacts
It forbids killing animals and cares for stray dogs during hard times
It limits tourism strictly to guided tours to protect the environment
questions.explain: The passage says Bhutan is carbon-negative because its forests absorb more CO2 than its populace emits.

questions.q: What is the purpose of Gelephu Mindfulness City?
options: An economic hub around innovation that preserves tradition and may keep young people home
A new capital designed to relocate the king's government to the southern border
A luxury resort district meant to draw foreign tourists to Bhutan's temples
A pilgrimage center that would double the number of Buddhist monks in the country
questions.explain: The king plans it as an innovation hub preserving tradition, because young people are leaving to find opportunity.

questions.q: Why does the author mostly believe what he heard about Bhutan's king?
options: The king personally told him the stories
He considers the situation unlike North Korea's
The tour guide showed him official records
The UN had confirmed the stories
questions.explain: He contrasts North Korean claims, saying the situations are wildly different and he is inclined to mostly believe Bhutan's.
